title: Bring It Over: The Food Counter's Own Word

lessons.title: Hear lāvo — bring it
lessons.gloss: bring it — the asking word a food counter needs

segments.text: Recall the closing payoff and the three-word transport payoff, then write bus and make it.
lāvo — bring it.
Two beats, and the fourth asking word in this track. Say them in the order you met them: dikhāvo, karo, lo, do, lāvo. Every one ends the same way.
lāvo is the one a food counter needs. You do not ask for tea to be shown to you; you ask for it to be brought. The source prints it with a food word, which is exactly where the next lesson puts it.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6.

segments.prompt: Which asking word would you use for tea, dikhāvo or lāvo?

feedback.correct: Right: tea is brought, not shown.
feedback.incorrect: dikhāvo shows a thing where it stands; lāvo carries it over.

lessons.title: लावो (lāvo) — bring it, on the page
lessons.gloss: bring it, written from three signs and the ending every asking word shares

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say bring it, then write wind and show it.
ला + वो becomes लावो — lāvo — bring it.

Three signs, none new. Its ending वो is the same one that closes दिखावो. Write लो and लावो (lāvo) one under the other: same first letter, and everything after it is what separates taking from bringing.
Look at the pair, cover it, wait five seconds, and write both from their meanings: first take it, then bring it.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6.

segments.prompt: From lāvo, write the word that asks for something to be brought over.

feedback.correct: Right: ला, then the वो that also ends दिखावो.

lessons.title: Hear chāy lāvo — bring tea
lessons.gloss: bring tea — the request a food counter actually hears

segments.text: Recall the seven-word food payoff, say the request from Chapter 26, then write the sweet crumbled wheat dessert, tea, and bring it.
chāy lāvo — bring tea.

Two words. The food comes first and the asking word last, the same order you already use in ye kapṛā dikhāvo, with the pointing word left out because you are not choosing between cups in front of you.
Any of the seven food words fits the first slot. Say the line three times, with chāy, then roṭī, then dāl, and notice that nothing else in it moves.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6.

segments.prompt: What does chāy lāvo ask for?

feedback.correct: Right: the food word first, the asking word last.
feedback.incorrect: Two words only: chāy, then lāvo.

lessons.title: चाय लावो। (chāy lāvo.) — the order on the page
lessons.gloss: bring tea, written from two words already written

segments.text: Write ट, then write flatbread and hard wheat rolls.
चाय | लावो (lāvo)।.
Two written words and a stop. Now write the same line twice more, replacing चाय with रोटी and then with बाटी. Only the first word changes, and you have written all three of those words before.
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write it. Then write the two variants from memory and check that लावो (lāvo) is identical in all three.
Source: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6.

segments.prompt: Write the line that orders tea.

feedback.correct: Food word first, asking word last, stop at the end.
feedback.incorrect: Rebuild one word at a time: चाय | लावो।

lessons.title: Retrieve bring it against the other four
lessons.gloss: the bringing word and the order it makes

segments.text: Write very and a little, then say which one makes a description stronger.

Five asking words are now in play. Hear them shuffled and give each meaning. Read five cards: दिखावो, करो, लो, दो, लावो (lāvo). Write all five from sound, then write the tea order and say which of the five it uses.
Sources: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6; Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9.

segments.prompt: Write bring it, then the whole tea order.

feedback.correct: The word and the order both come back separately.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed one, then write the pair again.

lessons.title: Payoff — five asking words, five jobs
lessons.gloss: five asking words, each matched to the counter it belongs at

segments.text: Recall the three-counter request payoff and write the request itself.
All five end in the same sound and none of them is interchangeable.
Hear all five shuffled and name each one's job.
Produce all five from their jobs alone, without the sounds.
Read five cards and match each to one line you already know.
Write all five from dictation, then write the tea order, the counter-offer, and the closing question that asks for a final price.
Pass each skill separately. Five ways to ask is not five ways to be understood: refusing, thanking somebody for doing it, and asking again more softly are all still untaught.
Sources: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6; Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9.

segments.prompt: Complete all four scored checks, then write the asking word a food counter needs.

feedback.correct: Five asking words now pass separately in four skills.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the failed skill or word, then retry that part.

lessons.title: Close the writing loop for ल, व and च
lessons.gloss: delayed closure for three consonants the asking words lean on

segments.text: Recall the five-word asking payoff, then write child and wind.
Write five single signs from sound cues: ल, व, च, छ, ख. Two of those five are breathed partners of the two before them; say all five and mark which two carry the breath.
Then write लावो, लो, दिखावो, चाय लावो। (chāy lāvo.), and पाछे मिलसू from dictation. Repair only the missed sign and rewrite its word once.
Sources: Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6; Unicode Devanagari chart.

segments.prompt: Write the plain ch, then its breathed partner.

feedback.correct: Both close on their own, away from the words that carry them.
feedback.incorrect: Say both aloud with a hand at your mouth; the breathed one is छ.
